facts.statement: Xinjiangovenator is a genus of coelurosaurian dinosaurs that may belong to the group Maniraptora.
facts.quote: Xinjiangovenator (meaning "Xinjiang hunter") is a genus of coelurosaurian dinosaurs, possibly part of the group Maniraptora

facts.statement: The remains of Xinjiangovenator were first described by Dong Zhiming in 1973 from fossils found in the Lianmuqin Formation of Wuerho, Xinjiang, China.
facts.quote: The remains of Xinjiangovenator were found in the Lianmuqin Formation of Wuerho, Xinjiang, China, and were first described by Dong Zhiming in 1973

facts.statement: The genus is based on a single holotype specimen consisting of an articulated partial right lower leg including the tibia, fibula fragments, ankle bones, and fused foot bones.
facts.quote: The genus is based on a single specimen, an articulated partial right lower leg, containing the tibia, three pieces of the fibula, the calcaneum and the astragalus, as well as two fused pedal phalanges

facts.statement: Oliver Rauhut and Xu Xing established the new genus Xinjiangovenator in 2005 after realizing the holotype hindlimb bones could not be assigned to the tooth-based genus Phaedrolosaurus.
facts.quote: The holotype was originally thought to be another specimen of Phaedrolosaurus. However, Phaedrolosaurus is based only on a non-diagnostic tooth, so the hindlimb bones were given their own genus by Oliver Rauhut and Xu Xing in 2005

facts.statement: The holotype's lower leg, comprising the tibia and ankle bones, measures 31.2 cm in length.
facts.quote: The lower leg (tibia plus ankle bones) has a length of 31.2 cm

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated in 2010 that individuals of this genus reached a length of 3 meters and a mass of 70 kilograms.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul estimated in 2010 that individuals of this genus had a length of 3 m and a mass of 70 kg

facts.statement: Rauhut and Xu identified a unique trait where the lateral ankle joint at the bottom of the tibia extends further back than the outer edge of the tibia near the knee.
facts.quote: First, the lateral condyle (outer ankle joint) at the lower end of the tibia extends further backwards than the outer edge of the portion of the tibia near the knee

facts.statement: A second unique trait is a longitudinal groove along the front edge of the upper part of the fibula near the knee.
facts.quote: Secondly, the proximal part of the fibula (near the knee) has a longitudinal groove along its front edge

facts.statement: Rauhut and Xu originally placed Xinjiangovenator within the Maniraptora subgroup of coelurosaurs based on a phylogenetic analysis in 2005.
facts.quote: Rauhut & Xu (2005) originally placed Xinjiangovenator within the coelurosaur subgroup Maniraptora using a phylogenetic analysis

facts.statement: The analysis suggested Xinjiangovenator was more closely related to paravians like dromaeosaurids and birds than to oviraptorosaurians and therizinosaurs.
facts.quote: It was considered to be more closely related to paravians such as dromaeosaurids and birds, rather than oviraptorosaurians and therizinosaurs

facts.statement: Some phylogenetic trees suggest Xinjiangovenator is the sister taxon to Ornitholestes, based on the upper tibia being equally wide at the front and rear edges.
facts.quote: Some, but not all, of the phylogenetic trees found Xinjiangovenator as the sister taxon to Ornitholestes based on the proximal part of the tibia being just as wide along its front edge as its rear edge

facts.statement: Xinjiangovenator lived between 137.05 and 100.5 million years ago, spanning the Valanginian to Albian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Valanginian to Albian (137.05 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is debated whether Xinjiangovenator is a basal maniraptoran, as removing it from analysis revealed Ornitholestes to be the basal form instead.
facts.quote: When Xinjiangovenator was removed from the analysis, Ornitholestes was found to be a basal maniraptoran

rejected.statement: A 2010 analysis found Xinjiangovenator to have an unstable phylogenetic position within Coelurosauria due to its fragmentary nature.
rejected.quote: Due to its fragmentary nature, Xinjiangovenator was found to have an unstable position within Coelurosauria

rejected.statement: Xinjiangovenator lived in China during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically between the Valanginian and Albian stages.
rejected.quote: Xinjiangovenator ... lived in the Lianmuqin Formation of the Tugulu Group of China, dated to the Early Cretaceous period, sometime between the Valanginian and Albian stages
